title: Streamed JSON graceful-degrade & call-boundary protocol for truncation/escape/resume
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: clients occasionally receive truncated or partially-escaped JSON when model output is streamed and an upstream interruption (network, preemption, OOM) occurs. This is especially problematic when tool/function calls are emitted mid-stream: downstream plugins expect a complete JSON object and fail hard on malformed fragments. Goal: define a compact, backward-compatible protocol and server-side behavior that enables (1) graceful degradation for legacy clients, (2) precise resumption semantics for new clients with continuation tokens, and (3) deterministic tool-call boundaries so retries and idempotent replays are safe.
background: We already have several fixes for streaming truncation and framing heuristics in ad-hoc form (escape suffix insertion, sentinel tokens). Those fixes are fragile across SDK versions and complicate toolcalling. This ticket synthesizes a single protocol (framing-negotiation + continuation tokens + boundary-sentinels) and implementation plan for runtime-2.4, plus SDK compatibility rules. It must interoperate with Dedicated & Private deployments where proxies may strip unknown headers.
acceptance_criteria: Define framing negotiation: server announces supported modes; clients may request mode via 'X-Redwood-Stream-Mode' header. Modes: 'ldjson-legacy', 'sentinel-v1', 'manifested-chunks'.
Design continuation token format (short TTL, HMAC) that encodes last-safe-offset, active tool-call id, and model-version; token is restartable and idempotent on server-side.

Tool-call boundary rule: model-emitted tool calls must be wrapped with explicit boundary entries (sentinel 'TOOL_BEGIN' + metadata + 'TOOL_END') in 'sentinel-v1' and with manifest entries for 'manifested-chunks'.

Fallback behaviour: for clients that accept only 'ldjson-legacy', server must append an escape suffix and a deterministic 'truncation_hint' JSON field when truncation occurs so downstream parsers can detect incomplete objects without raising fatal errors.
SDKs (js, python) updated to honor negotiation header and to attempt resume using continuation token on retry with exponential backoff; unit/integration tests added.
Benchmark: resume flow round-trip adds <10ms median overhead and reduces client-visible failures by >=60% on simulated preemption tests.
Docs: Confluence design doc + example server logs + sample SDK usage snippets published and linked from API docs.
Canary: rollout to 5% hosted traffic then 25% with observability flags; rollback criteria defined in rollout playbook.

notes: Trade-offs discussed in design doc: sentinel-v1 increases payload by ~0.2% but gives unambiguous boundaries for toolcalls. Manifested-chunks is optimal for high-throughput batching but requires upstream proxies to preserve chunk-ordering; not enabled for Private by default. Continuation tokens carry minimal state to avoid long-term storage; short TTLs (30s) recommended. Security: HMAC protects token replay within TTL; ensure KMS rotation is handled.
